title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse failure, not a model error or an impersonation. A person with legitimate credentials used law enforcement systems, a camera network, a license plate reader and a state criminal database, for purposes the systems were not built to serve. The access itself was authorised, which is what makes this class of failure hard to see from the outside.

The misuse is alleged to have run from April 10 to May 1, 2024, a span of roughly three weeks. Catching it would have required comparing queries and camera or tag reader lookups against documented casework, and doing so on a timescale short enough to interrupt the pattern rather than reconstruct it afterward. The investigation that followed was multi-year and began only after the sheriff requested it.

The indictment is an allegation, not a finding. Rozar has not been convicted, and no determination of intent has been established.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A woman who says she was tracked by former Coffee County deputy Chris Ashley Rozar has spoken out anonymously. She said she hopes her story helps other women report abuse. A Coffee County grand jury indicted Rozar on eight counts, including four counts of violating his oath, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say he misused sheriff's office camera, tag reader, and GCIC database systems for personal reasons, not law enforcement, between April 10 and May 1, 2024.

The Georgia Bureau of Investigation led the multi-year investigation after former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested it in 2024. Rozar was terminated when the investigation began. He was arrested on May 5 on bench warrants and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
